stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Predicts Pakistan Will Join Major Global Economies Before 2050
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan is on track to become one of the world's major economies before 2050. Speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 on Friday, he pointed to a Goldman Sachs projection suggesting the country could rank as the sixth-largest economy globally by 2075. The prime minister emphasized that Pakistan is steering its economic trajectory toward growth and transformation, shifting away from the export of raw minerals in favor of utilizing these resources for domestic downstream industries.

Highlighting specific natural wealth, PM Shehbaz pointed to the Reko Diq project, recognized as one of the largest undeveloped deposits of copper and gold globally. After stalling for two decades, the project is advancing toward operational completion. To support the sector, authorities have established the National Minerals Data Centre and digitized geological records to ensure access to authentic information. Furthermore, the prime minister assured the business community of comprehensive government support, highlighting that protecting investors and local communities is a top priority for ensuring project success.

Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir also addressed the forum, stating that Pakistan aims to position itself as a competitive hub for long-term mineral investment. He noted that the national objective encompasses developing the entire value chain—including refining and manufacturing—rather than merely exporting raw materials. Adequate security measures will be implemented across the entire mining ecosystem to safeguard mines, miners, investments, and supply routes.

Both leaders stressed that mineral development must yield tangible improvements for local communities living in resource-rich areas. Field Marshal Munir noted that the country must transition from potential to productivity and from promises to action. The forum underscores a collaborative effort between federal and provincial governments to enhance infrastructure, boost productivity, and foster sustainable economic partnerships.

stories.title: Pakistan to Host FIH Men's Nations Cup in Lahore for 2027
stories.summary:
Pakistan is set to host the International Hockey Federation (FIH) Men’s Nations Cup in Lahore from February 19 to 28, 2027. This marks the country's first time hosting a major FIH event in 24 years. The agreement was officially signed by FIH President Tayyab Ikram and interim Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) President Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani during a ceremony in Islamabad on Friday.

The tournament will expand from eight to ten teams for its fifth edition. Alongside host Pakistan, participating countries include Egypt, Ireland, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Scotland, South Africa, South Korea, and the United States. Pakistan, who finished as runners-up in the previous 2024-25 edition, aims to use home advantage to secure promotion to the elite 2027-28 FIH Hockey Pro League.

During the announcement, Ikram praised Pakistan's hockey talent and confirmed that the Naseer Bunda Hockey Stadium has been approved as an official FIH High Performance Centre. Federal ministers Rana Sanaullah Khan and Attaullah Tarar also attended the event, reiterating the government's commitment to supporting the national sport and addressing structural and financial reforms within the federation.

Launched in 2022, the Nations Cup gives emerging hockey nations high-level competition and a merit-based pathway to the Pro League. Previous editions took place in South Africa, Poland, and Malaysia. The upcoming 10-day tournament in Lahore will provide Pakistan with an opportunity to demonstrate its capacity to host major international sporting events.

stories.title: Kuwait Announces Scheduled Power Outages Across Nine Districts for Maintenance
stories.summary:
Kuwait's Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy has announced scheduled, temporary power outages affecting nine residential districts across multiple governorates. The maintenance work is scheduled to begin at 8:00 AM on Saturday and last for a total of four hours.

According to ministry representatives, the temporary disruptions are an essential part of a periodic technical maintenance program. Engineers will inspect secondary substations to enhance their operational efficiency, ensure extended operation, and maintain grid stability. While officials aim to complete the work within four hours, timelines may vary slightly based on field conditions.

The affected residential sectors include specific blocks in Al-Shaab 1, Al-Dhahr 6, Al-Nahda 3, Sulaibikhat 2, Rumaithiya 9, Qurtuba 4, Al-Farwaniya 2, Al-Farwaniya 4, and Abdullah Mubarak Al-Sabah 6. The exact dates of disruption depend on utility conditions and may occur within the upcoming weeks or face postponement.

Residents and commercial establishments located within the designated blocks have been advised to exercise caution ahead of the morning disruptions. The ministry reaffirmed its objective to balance the electrical network's load and minimize inconvenience while carrying out infrastructure modernization to meet Kuwait's growing energy needs.

stories.title: German Envoy Highlights Trade Growth and Warns of Global Conflicts
stories.summary:
German Consul General Thomas Schultze expressed concern over the Russia-Ukraine war during a reception in Karachi, stating that the conflict has threatened peace beyond Europe and undermined hopes for a more peaceful world. However, he emphasized that historical reconciliation between Germany and France proves former adversaries can build lasting friendships and economic cooperation.

The reception celebrated 75 years of diplomatic relations between Germany and Pakistan. Schultze noted that bilateral trade grew from approximately one billion euros in 1990 to 3.7 billion euros in 2025. He added that the European Union is Pakistan's largest export partner, with bilateral trade reaching nearly $14 billion and giving Pakistan a trade surplus of around $6 billion.

Highlighting historical ties, Schultze recalled the 1870 Indo-European telegraph line connecting Europe with Karachi and Bombay, and Siemens opening its first local office in Lahore in 1922. He also noted cultural connections, including national poet Allama Muhammad Iqbal’s studies in Germany and German-born Dr. Ruth Pfau's 55 years of work fighting leprosy in Pakistan.

Economic cooperation between the two nations dates back to 1961, with Germany allocating about $4.3 billion in assistance focused on climate, energy, sustainable development, and vocational training. Schultze also mentioned the recent visit of President Asif Ali Zardari and Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah to Germany, which is expected to expand the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) activities in Sindh.

stories.title: African Contestants Face Travel Delays and Withdrawals from Miss Universe
stories.summary:
Tighter American travel policies and recent executive orders implemented by the Trump administration have caused severe travel delays and restrictions for African contestants heading to the Miss Universe pageant. The administrative hurdles have forced some delegates to withdraw entirely from the international competition, while others remain in limbo.

National directors have officially withdrawn contestants from Zambia and the Republic of Congo due to entry barriers. Mubanga Pamela Hatyoka, the national titleholder for Zambia, and Georgina Kambongo, who made history as the first-ever representative for the Republic of Congo, will both be unable to attend despite rigorous preparation.

Meanwhile, Zimbabwean delegate Roseanna Hall and South Sudanese hopeful Adut Deng have spent over six months battling bureaucratic hurdles and are still anxiously awaiting travel approval. National representatives emphasized that these delegates are filled with enthusiasm and pride to represent their countries on a global platform.

The visa and travel complications add to ongoing tensions between international cultural events and national immigration policies. Delegates are scheduled to gather in Puerto Rico for preliminary competitions, national costume events, and rehearsals ahead of the final pageant crown.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Suspends Local Government Election Schedule
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court has halted the local government election schedule in the federal capital by issuing a stay order against a notification released by the Election Commission of Pakistan on October 21. Justice Umair Majeed Malik announced the reserved verdict following a petition filed by Amjad Ali, who argued that new delimitation occurred in 2024 before a new Local Government Ordinance was introduced in 2026. According to the petitioner's counsel, the election schedule was issued without restoring previous delimitations after that ordinance ceased to operate. In addition to halting the schedule, the court issued a notice to the Election Commission of Pakistan, instructing the body to submit a response by November 26.

This legal development unfolds against a backdrop of prolonged delays in local governance within the Islamabad Capital Territory. The tenure of the previous elected local government system concluded in February 2021, but fresh polls could not take place previously due to various legal and administrative challenges. Under Section 219, subsection 4, of the Elections Act of 2017, the electoral watchdog is legally required to conduct new local government elections within 120 days after a term expires.

The suspension coincides with rising tensions between the electoral authority and the federal administration regarding the upcoming vote. Just a day prior to the court's decision, Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja accused the federal government of attempting to sabotage the scheduled local government polls in Islamabad. He headed a three-member bench hearing a case concerning code of conduct violations in the recent Gujranwala NA-77 by-election when he raised these concerns. The Chief Election Commissioner took strict notice of government orders prohibiting teachers from serving election duties, questioning where the commission would source its staff and asserting that directives flow from the commission to the government rather than the reverse. Despite these hurdles, he maintained that the municipal elections would proceed as planned.

stories.title: Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online Outage Triggers Estimated $700 Million in Insured Losses
stories.summary:
Insured losses stemming from the recent Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online outage are projected to reach approximately $700 million, according to a preliminary assessment by Shalom Bublil, co-founder and chief product officer at Kovrr. The technical disruption began at 1617 GMT on Thursday, and Bublil's initial estimate ranges from $300 million to $1.4 billion, assuming the system issues were resolved by 1900 GMT on Friday. This projection is built on an estimated $16 billion in economic losses tied to lost productivity.

The wide gap between economic and insured losses highlights the restrictions inherent in many cyber insurance policies regarding accidental or non-malicious failures at third-party technology providers. Furthermore, low cyber insurance adoption rates among small businesses contribute to the lower insured total. Market sources compared the potential claims to the July 2024 CrowdStrike outage, for which reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter previously estimated insured losses at roughly $250 million.

Microsoft reported steady recovery across affected regions by Friday afternoon, though the tech giant noted that some users might still encounter intermittent access delays or email issues. The company confirmed there was no evidence pointing to malicious activity. Industry experts, including Tom Dryden of McGill and Partners, noted that coverage depends heavily on policy wording, such as dependent business interruption provisions and the inclusion of non-malicious system failures.

Navigating these claims presents unique obstacles for professional services firms, where email disruptions may delay daily work tasks without causing permanent revenue losses if employees can catch up later. Insurers may also enforce waiting periods lasting between 8 and 12 hours before business interruption coverage activates. While insurers monitor the systemic nature of the incident closely, industry professionals emphasize that it remains early to determine the final volume and exact scale of the claims.

stories.title: Punjab Completes 128-Kilometre Lillah-Jhelum Road Project After Five Years of Construction
stories.summary:
The 128-kilometre Lillah-Jhelum Road project in Pakistan's Punjab province has officially been completed five years after its initial launch in 2021. The major infrastructure development is designed to significantly improve transit connectivity for local residents living in Jhelum and Pind Dadan Khan.

Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif formally congratulated the Communication and Works (C&W) Department on the successful completion of the initiative. During a recent official briefing, she directed relevant administrative officials to accelerate ongoing construction work on the adjacent Jhelum-Pind Dadan Khan Road to maintain momentum in regional transport upgrades.

Built as a dual carriageway at a total cost of Rs. 13.538 billion, the newly finished infrastructure connects Pind Dadan Khan directly to the Lillah Interchange. To facilitate smoother traffic flow and accommodate higher commuting volumes, the existing road width was expanded from its previous 20 to 24 feet up to 76 feet. The construction was organized into five distinct sections to guarantee timely delivery, incorporating a 4.2-kilometre Jalalpur bypass and a 3.98-kilometre Pind Dadan Khan bypass.

Additional structural features of the project include 185 small bridges and paved shoulders designed to strengthen the road edges. Three remaining culverts are also scheduled for completion shortly. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz emphasized that her administration is making historic strides in regional transport by constructing, expanding, and rehabilitating 35,000 kilometres of rural link roads across the province to bolster local economic activity.

stories.title: Federal Government Extends Civil Servants' Digital Asset Declaration Deadline to November 30
stories.summary:
The federal government has officially extended the deadline for civil servants to digitally submit their mandatory declarations of assets for the 2025-26 financial year. Under the updated schedule, employees now have until November 30, 2026, to file their financial disclosures through the Federal Board of Revenue portal.

The timeline adjustment was formalized through an Office Memorandum issued by the Establishment Division. According to the announcement, the deadline relaxation received direct approval from the Prime Minister as a formal relaxation of Rule 12(6) of the Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules for 2026. This supersedes the initial submission deadline that was previously communicated to government personnel in an Office Memorandum dated September 16, 2026.

In addition to extending the primary filing window, the government has provided extra time for personnel to make necessary corrections to their submitted declarations. Civil servants can now submit amendments until December 31, 2026, provided they secure formal approval from their respective Cadre Administrator.

To enforce compliance across the public sector, the Establishment Division has instructed all ministries, divisions, and cadre administrators to distribute the updated directives immediately. Administrative heads are tasked with ensuring that all officers under their supervision complete the digital submission process before the newly established November 30 deadline.

stories.title: India's Merchandise Trade Deficit Reaches One-Year High of $39.88 Billion in October
stories.summary:
India's merchandise trade deficit widened significantly in October to a one-year high of $39.88 billion, surpassing market forecasts and increasing from September's deficit of $30.21 billion. The surge was primarily driven by a substantial spike in gold imports ahead of the Diwali festival, alongside heightened energy import costs stemming from ongoing Middle East conflicts.

Gold imports more than tripled to $5.51 billion in October, rising sharply from $1.8 billion in September as domestic jewellers and consumers increased purchases during the festive season. To curb investment demand, India's market regulator had previously nudged asset management firms in mid-October to halt bulk purchases of gold exchange-traded funds. Meanwhile, petroleum product imports climbed 54.31% year-on-year to $22.82 billion, reflecting high global prices as the Indian crude basket neared $120 a barrel before Brent crude futures subsequently declined to around $95 a barrel.

Despite the rising import bill, total merchandise exports reached $49.47 billion in October, up from $44.4 billion in September. Trade Secretary Rajesh Agrawal noted that India recorded its highest-ever monthly goods exports during the month, bolstered by increased shipments of petroleum, electronics, engineering goods, and gems and jewellery. Cumulative goods and services exports from April through October rose 16.66% year-on-year to $568.84 billion, while imports grew 16% to $662.19 billion, pushing the overall trade deficit to $93.35 billion.

Bilateral trade discussions between India and the United States remain active as both nations work toward finalizing the first tranche of a trade deal. Concurrently, the United States maintained its position as India's top export market, with exports totaling $59.52 billion between April and October. Additionally, India's robust services sector generated an estimated $40.51 billion in exports against $20.72 billion in imports for October, resulting in a healthy services trade surplus of $19.79 billion.

stories.title: Microsoft Reports Recovery Signs After Global Outlook and Teams Outage
stories.summary:
Microsoft stated on Friday that it was seeing improvements for Outlook email and other productivity tools following a major international outage that disrupted businesses and government agencies for over twelve hours. The disruption crippled communications globally, forcing some organizations to use fax machines and halting a bond repurchase transaction in Europe. According to the company, server issues were the root cause of the incident, which also impacted the Copilot AI assistant, while software fixes were deployed to stabilize the system. Microsoft noted that it had no indication of any malicious activity.

The widespread disruption affected essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars, and holding virtual meetings across multiple continents. Public statements revealed that government bodies, trading firms, airlines, and financial institutions in regions ranging from the United States and Europe to Australia and Japan experienced communication delays or restricted access. Organizations hosting Microsoft services on their own servers rather than relying on the cloud were largely spared. Monitoring platform Downdetector recorded tens of thousands of reports concerning Outlook problems in the United States and various Asia-Pacific countries.

The incident specifically impaired features tied to Exchange Online, the cloud-based messaging and scheduling hub of Microsoft 365, while unconnected applications remained functional. This event marks one of the longest outages in the company's history and follows previous service disruptions earlier in the year and late last year. Industry analysts noted that recurring reliability issues could prompt IT departments to reconsider their heavy reliance on a single major technology provider, despite the significant switching costs involved in replacing deeply embedded workplace tools.

Numerous high-profile organizations reported operational hurdles due to the technical failure. In the United Kingdom, the National Health Service turned to paper records and alternate IT systems, while the Metropolitan Police faced difficulties regarding online crime reporting. European exchange operator Euronext, British insurer Aviva, Danish shipping giant Maersk, and various international airlines and financial firms also encountered service disruptions. Australian Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke stated that Microsoft did not suspect a cyberattack, comparing the situation to previous software update failures.

stories.title: PSW and Alibaba.com Launch Digital Trade Data Confirmation Service
stories.summary:
Pakistan Single Window and Alibaba.com have officially entered into an agreement to launch a digital Trade Data Confirmation Service. This initiative merges Pakistan's digital trade infrastructure with the global business-to-business marketplace of Alibaba.com to enhance trust and encourage greater participation of Pakistani enterprises in international e-commerce. The announcement was detailed in a statement released on Friday.

Under this new arrangement, the service introduces an additional layer of verification for Alibaba.com and its worldwide buyers. The confirmation process will operate through Application Programming Interface-based requests and responses, ensuring that the underlying trade data is not directly transferred or exchanged. By enabling independent digital confirmation of export declarations, the service aims to reinforce buyer confidence in local suppliers and increase transparency across supply chain transactions.

Syed Aftab Haider, the Chief Executive Officer of Pakistan Single Window, highlighted that the collaboration demonstrates how national digital trade infrastructure can foster innovative services for cross-border commerce. He noted that utilizing API integration optimizes trade data use, thereby strengthening the integrity and reliability of businesses within the country. The partnership represents a cooperative model between private digital platforms and government-mandated single window systems.

Summer Gao, Head of Pakistan Business at Alibaba.com, stated that the initiative will help Pakistani exporters conduct business more seamlessly with international buyers. She emphasized that the service establishes a new benchmark for reliability and transparency in global e-commerce, offering robust support for local businesses as they seek to expand their footprint in international markets.

stories.title: Barrick Mining Expresses Interest in Processing Industries in Karachi and Gwadar
stories.summary:
Representatives from Barrick Mining Corporation expressed strong interest in investing in mineral processing industries situated in Karachi and Gwadar. The announcement took place on Friday during a meeting in Islamabad between a visiting delegation led by Chairman John Thornton and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to an official statement released by the Prime Minister's Office on X.

During the discussions, the delegation praised the government's decision to organize a minerals conference, viewing it as a significant step forward for mineral development in the country. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif emphasized that Pakistan possesses vast natural resources and mineral wealth, noting that harnessing these assets to foster regional development and improve public prosperity remains a top priority. He highlighted that major ventures like the Reko Diq project will generate employment opportunities, skills development, and economic growth, particularly for the people of Balochistan.

The prime minister stated that the successful execution of the Reko Diq project will establish a benchmark for future mineral investments in Pakistan. He added that the government is actively cultivating a favorable environment focused on trade, investment, infrastructure, and modern technology to support the sector. Furthermore, the meeting addressed appropriate policy, regulatory, and infrastructure frameworks designed to encourage long-term development within Pakistan's mineral industry.

The Reko Diq mine stands as one of the largest underdeveloped copper-gold deposits globally, with projections suggesting substantial future cash flows. The project is jointly owned by Canadian mining titan Barrick Mining Corporation alongside the federal and Balochistan governments. Industry sources indicate that production at the site might face a two-year delay until 2030, pending improvements in regional security and de-escalation of the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Nvidia Names Interim CEO Colette Kress Following Jensen Huang's Departure Amid Scandals
stories.summary:
Nvidia has appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO following the departure of co-founder Jensen Huang, who stepped down after leading the chipmaker for three decades. Huang's exit follows a cloud of scandal involving a relationship with an executive who reported to him, alongside scrutiny over massive financing deals that critics labeled a circular AI economy. Kress, 59, previously served as a vital counterweight to Huang's risky financial ambitions and large investments in startups and AI infrastructure.

During her tenure as finance chief, Kress and her team frequently clashed with Huang over aggressive financing strategies, such as backing an OpenAI data center project in Ohio that was ultimately scaled down. Known for her pragmatic and calming demeanor, Kress has already engaged with customers and suppliers to stabilize markets amidst the recent leadership turmoil. Industry observers suggest her leadership style may lead Nvidia to adopt a more conventional approach toward Washington policymakers regarding export controls.

Despite her extensive experience with major tech firms like Microsoft, Cisco, and Texas Instruments, industry analysts question whether a finance executive can sustain Nvidia's aggressive technological risk-taking. Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 and saw her equity value rise significantly, placing her among America's richest self-made women by mid-2026. Whether she will retain the top position permanently remains undecided, with other names such as Ian Buck, Lisa Su, and Rene Haas also circulating as potential successors.

The leadership transition comes at a sensitive time for the company. Nvidia shares experienced a significant downturn following the announcement of Huang's departure before paring some losses. Additionally, questions remain regarding oversight of chip sales involving Chinese military-linked entities, an area where Kress could potentially face congressional inquiries.

stories.title: Grassroots Climate Activists Face Severe Funding and Access Hurdles Attending UN COP Summits
stories.summary:
Young grassroots climate activists from rural and marginalized communities face profound bureaucratic, financial, and logistical barriers when attempting to secure participation at United Nations climate conferences. Maryam Jamali, a 23-year-old climate activist and co-founder of Madat Balochistan, observed that while international climate discussions frequently center on vulnerable regions like Pakistan, individuals directly affected by catastrophes on the ground are rarely present at the negotiating tables.

Jamali's experience highlights the immense difficulty of navigating international accreditation and funding processes. After applying for multiple COP summits, she managed to secure a conference badge for COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, through a sponsoring organization and a friend. However, she struggled to raise the necessary travel funds through online crowdfunding, falling short of the required amount. Similarly, Aitzaz Roonjha, an 18-year-old activist from Lasbela, Balochistan, was selected to attend COP30 but could not participate due to a complete lack of financial assistance for travel, accommodation, and visas.

Activists point out that access to these global forums often relies heavily on personal connections and urban-centric organizational affiliations, rendering events largely inaccessible to working-class individuals from frontline regions. While youth-led organizations like Climate Forward Pakistan (CFP) assist delegates with documentation, visas, and accreditation, they typically do not cover travel and meal expenses, leaving participants responsible for securing their own funding. CFP founding director Durlabh Ashok notes that avoiding grant-driven operations helps prevent undue influence over funding decisions, but this model inevitably places financial burdens on delegates.

Although UNFCCC rules do not explicitly mandate privileged backgrounds for participation, observer organizations must navigate limited quotas and a lack of dedicated trust funds for observer financial support. Consequently, representatives from developing countries and marginalized areas continue to face steep obstacles in turning formal selections into actual attendance at major climate summits.

stories.title: Election Commission of Pakistan Gives Government Two Weeks to Request Cantonment Board Polls
stories.summary:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has granted the Prime Minister's Office a strict two-week deadline to submit a formal written request for holding local government elections across 42 cantonment boards nationwide. Headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, a five-member ECP bench issued an order warning that failure to respond within the stipulated period will force the commission to pass appropriate legal orders.

Local government terms in the cantonment boards expired on April 11, making elections due by August 8 under Section 219(4) of the Elections Act, 2017. Although the ECP completed the delimitation of wards by April 20 and held consultative meetings with the Ministry of Defence and the Military Lands and Cantonments Department (ML&CD), the necessary formal request from the federal government under Section 19-D(2) of the Cantonments Act, 1924, has remained pending despite numerous letters, reminders, and formal hearings.

During recent proceedings, representatives for the defence ministry and the ML&CD confirmed their readiness to conduct the elections and stated that the required summary had already been forwarded to the federal government. They explained that delays occurred because senior leadership was preoccupied with critical national and international affairs. Nevertheless, the ECP emphasized that constitutional obligations under Articles 140-A and 219(d) require the commission to hold local government elections without undue delay.

The 42 cantonment boards span across all four provinces, including 20 in Punjab, 11 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 8 in Sindh, and 3 in Balochistan. The ECP has instructed its office to formally approach the Prime Minister's Office once again and relist the matter for a follow-up hearing after three weeks if no formal response is received.

stories.title: Global Microsoft Outage Cripples Businesses and Government Operations
stories.summary:
A severe Microsoft outage lasting more than 12 hours disrupted Outlook, Teams, and the Copilot AI assistant on Friday, crippling communications for corporations and governments globally. The technical failure prevented hundreds of millions of users from managing calendars, hosting virtual meetings, and sending emails, forcing some impacted entities to utilize fax machines or paper records.

The widespread disruption affected operations across multiple continents, impacting government agencies in Australia, Japan, and the United States, alongside trading firms, airlines, and financial institutions. Among the affected organizations were the UK’s National Health Service and Metropolitan Police, European exchange operator Euronext, Danish shipping giant Maersk, and British insurer Aviva. Additionally, American artificial intelligence firms OpenAI and Anthropic reported connection issues, while several Indian and Taiwanese companies experienced service disruptions.

Microsoft stated that server issues and traffic management imbalances specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online, its cloud-based messaging platform, while applications not relying on Exchange remained operational. Downdetector recorded tens of thousands of reports in the US and similar issues across the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia, and Japan. The company noted that it was not aware of any malicious activity, with Australian Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke confirming that officials believed the incident stemmed from an update gone awry rather than a cyberattack.

This incident represents one of the longest outages in Microsoft's history and follows previous service disruptions earlier in the year, including a January 305 failure and an Azure cloud platform outage last month. Market analysts noted that recurring reliability issues could prompt IT departments to reconsider relying on a single provider, though high switching costs remain a barrier. Microsoft shares fell 1.7 percent prior to the market opening, and the company stated it was shifting traffic to alternate routes and gradually restoring impacted servers.

stories.title: Asad Mahmood Fails to Attend NAB Hearing Over Postal Appointments
stories.summary:
Former federal minister Asad Mahmood did not appear before the National Accountability Bureau on November 13 despite receiving a fresh summons regarding an ongoing inquiry into alleged illegal appointments within the Pakistan Post Office Department. Neither Mahmood nor any legal representative attended the scheduled hearing at the bureau.

The investigation, led by NAB Rawalpindi, centers on alleged unlawful appointments involving various officers, employees, and individuals within the postal department. Mahmood previously served as the federal minister for Communications and Postal Services from 2022 to 2023, and is the son of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Fazal ur Rehman. Initially directed to appear in person on November 10, 2026, Mahmood instead submitted a written response through his lawyer.

After bureau officials deemed the written response unsatisfactory, a new notice was issued requiring his personal appearance on November 13 at 11 am. The summons warned that non-compliance could trigger legal action under Section 31 of the National Accountability Ordinance 1999. Following his latest absence, bureau sources indicated that decisions regarding whether to issue further summons would be made after consultations.

In a separate legal matter, Mahmood was previously declared a deliberate defaulter and absconder from investigation after failing to appear before the Federal Investigation Agency concerning a separate illegal recruitment case. Bureau officials are currently reviewing the next steps in the ongoing Pakistan Post Office inquiry.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Gains Over 500 Points to Close Higher
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange finished the trading session on a positive note on Friday, November 13, 2026, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index increasing by 500.11 points, representing a 0.28 percent rise. The index settled at 177,873.88 points, up from its previous closing of 177,373.76 points.

During the trading day, the benchmark index fluctuated, touching a session high of 179,284.34 points and dropping to a low of 176,865.05 points. Market breadth remained favorable on the Ready Market, where 284 companies registered gains while 184 declined, and 29 companies remained unchanged out of a total of 497 traded firms.

Trading activity on the Regular Market saw a turnover of 1,042,809,816 shares, lower than the 1,070,480,302 shares recorded in the preceding session. Total traded value also decreased to Rs. 31,001,378,645, compared to Rs. 31,636,479,275 previously.

Despite the slight decline in trading volume and value, the overall market capitalization expanded. Total market capitalization rose to Rs. 19,335,992,126,923, marking an increase from the Rs. 19,224,008,466,887 recorded during the previous trading session.

stories.title: Finance Minister Urges Banks to Expand Cashless Pakistan Initiative
stories.summary:
Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani visited the Pakistan Banks Association head office in Karachi to meet with bank presidents, chief executive officers, and chief digital officers regarding the Prime Minister’s Cashless Pakistan Initiative. The meeting was also attended by officials from the State Bank of Pakistan, the chief executive officer of Raast, and representatives from Karandaaz.

During the session, Minister Kayani briefed banking executives on progress achieved under the initiative, focusing on the wider adoption of digital payments and the ongoing digitization of government transactions. He outlined specific targets established for the 2026 fiscal year and urged financial institutions to assume a more active role in accelerating the transition toward a cashless economy. Furthermore, he highlighted government support mechanisms, including the Raast QR subsidy intended to lower merchant discount rate charges, noting that the Prime Minister decided to continue the subsidy to maintain momentum.

The Minister announced that the Prime Minister’s Cashless Committee is actively refining its focus and establishing new indicators to fast-track digital payment adoption. He directed the State Bank of Pakistan to conduct detailed consultations with chief digital officers alongside Raast and Karandaaz leadership to formulate practical recommendations. These consultations aim to enhance user experience across digital payment platforms, particularly QR transactions, and generate actionable strategies for the committee.

Concluding the visit, Minister Kayani commended the contributions of Karandaaz and thanked the Pakistan Banks Association for hosting the discussions. Association representatives expressed appreciation for the government's focus on the digital transformation agenda and reaffirmed the banking sector's dedication to supporting the national objective.

stories.title: Government Collects Rs381 Billion in Petroleum Levy During First Quarter
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government collected Rs381 billion from the public through the petroleum levy during the first quarter of the current fiscal year, marking an increase of Rs10 billion compared to the same period last year. These figures were detailed in the Fiscal Operations Report for the July-September period, released by the Ministry of Finance.

According to the official documents, the government also gathered Rs22 billion under the carbon levy and Rs9 billion through the Electric Vehicle Adoption Levy within the same three-month timeframe. Total government revenues for the first quarter reached Rs6,003 billion, while total expenditures were recorded at Rs4,370 billion. The primary balance stood at Rs2,973 billion, which represents 2.7 percent of the Gross Domestic Product.

Expenditure figures within the ministry's report outlined several major allocations for the quarter. The government spent Rs1,700 billion on loan interest payments, Rs495 billion on defense expenditures, Rs263 billion on pensions, Rs206 billion on civil government expenses, and Rs84 billion on subsidies. Additionally, the State Bank of Pakistan generated a profit of Rs1,932 billion during the July-September period.

In separate infrastructure developments, the Ministry of Finance documents noted the completion of the 128-kilometer Lillah-Jhelum Road project five years after its initial launch in 2021. This project aims to enhance regional connectivity for residents residing in Jhelum and Pind Dadan Khan within the Punjab province. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif congratulated the Communication and Works Department on the completion and instructed officials to expedite ongoing work on other regional initiatives.

stories.title: Pakistan Seeks Long-Term Mineral Investment to Boost Economic Growth
stories.summary:
Pakistan is positioning itself to become a primary hub for long-term mineral investment, with a strong focus on community welfare, proper value addition, and enhanced security protocols. Speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir outlined the nation's strategic vision for the sector.

During his address, the field marshal assured that the entire mining ecosystem would receive comprehensive safeguarding, covering all associated personnel, industrial facilities, projects, and active mines. He noted that tapping into the country's mineral wealth represents a united national goal aimed at building lasting economic partnerships rather than merely shipping out untreated raw goods.

Emphasizing the importance of processing and manufacturing, the military leader stressed that the strategy must transition from raw material exports toward comprehensive value-added growth. He pointed out that transforming natural potential into actual productivity requires moving from empty promises to concrete actions across the nation.

Furthermore, the initiative places significant emphasis on local populations living near resource-rich zones, ensuring they experience tangible advancements in their daily lives. Highlighting the courage and determination of the Pakistani populace, the field marshal underscored that the country's true strength lies in its citizens rather than solely in its geological assets.

stories.title: Pakistan and Sri Lanka Draw First Test Following Weather Delays
stories.summary:
Pakistan secured a draw against Sri Lanka in the first Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday, aided by an impressive innings from Saud Shakeel and interruptions caused by bad weather. Sri Lanka had initially held a strong position in the match, reducing Pakistan to 151-5 at lunch on the fifth day with a 139-run lead. However, Shakeel played a crucial role by scoring 97 runs before being dismissed by Lahiru Kumara, falling just short of a century after making 93 in the first innings. 

Pakistan finished their second innings at 284-8, establishing a lead of 272 runs before both teams agreed to a draw. The home side's resistance was further supported by a 92-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Shakeel and Ghazi Ghori, who contributed 35 runs. Milan Rathnayaka was the pick of the Sri Lankan bowlers with figures of 3-47, while Asitha Fernando and Kumara claimed two and three wickets respectively. 

The match was heavily affected by adverse weather conditions throughout the week. Bad light repeatedly interrupted play during the final sessions of the first four days, resulting in the loss of 117 overs out of the scheduled 360, which significantly reduced the likelihood of a decisive result. On the fourth day, Sri Lanka had posted 446 all out in response to Pakistan's declared total of 434-9, largely due to a bowling performance by debutant Saqib Khan, who took 7-130. 

Earlier on the final day, Pakistan struggled as Babar Azam's long-standing century drought continued. Azam was caught for 34 off Rathnayaka, marking his 42nd consecutive Test innings without reaching the milestone. Salman Agha also fell for 13 to Rathnayaka, and early morning dismissals of Azan Awais and Mohammad Taha left the hosts under pressure. Both teams will now prepare for the second and final Test of the series, which begins at the same venue on Tuesday.

stories.title: نیوزی لینڈ کے ہاتھوں بھارت کو ون ڈے کی دوسری بڑی شکست
stories.summary:
نیوزی لینڈ کے شہر ماؤنٹ مونگانوئی میں کھیلے گئے ایک روزہ میچ میں میزبان ٹیم نے بھارت کو 244 رنز کے بھاری مارجن سے شکست دے دی ہے۔ یہ رنز کے اعتبار سے ون ڈے کرکٹ میں بھارت کی دوسری سب سے بڑی شکست ہے، جو کہ سنہ 2000 میں شارجہ کے مقام پر سری لنکا کے ہاتھوں ملنے والی 245 رنز کی شکست سے محض ایک رن کم ہے۔

میچ میں بھارت نے ٹاس جیت کر نیوزی لینڈ کو پہلے بیٹنگ کی دعوت دی۔ نیوزی لینڈ کے اوپنرز ول ینگ اور ٹِم سیفرٹ نے 85 رنز کی شراکت قائم کی، جبکہ ول ینگ نے شاندار بیٹنگ کرتے ہوئے اپنے کیریئر کی بہترین اننگز کھیلی اور 125 رنز بنائے۔ مقررہ 50 اوورز میں کیویز نے 10 وکٹوں کے نقصان پر 333 رنز بنائے۔ بھارت کی جانب سے عاقب نبی، گرنور برار اور اکشر پٹیل نے دو دو کھلاڑیوں کو آؤٹ کیا۔

ہدف کے تعاقب میں انڈین ٹیم کا آغاز انتہائی تباہ کن رہا جہاں میٹ ہنری نے پہلے ہی اوور میں روہت شرما، ویرات کوہلی اور شریاس اییر کو آؤٹ کر کے ٹیم کو صفر پر تین نقصان پہنچایا۔ میٹ ہنری نے مجموعی طور پر صرف 27 رنز دے کر چھ وکٹیں حاصل کیں۔ پوری انڈین ٹیم 27ویں اوور میں محض 89 رنز پر ڈھیر ہو گئی۔

اس بدترین شکست کے بعد سوشل میڈیا پر صارفین کی جانب سے انڈین ٹیم کی کارکردگی اور سلیکشن پر شدید تنقید کی گئی ہے۔ مداحوں نے اتنی بڑی شکست پر مایوسی کا اظہار کیا اور بالخصوص انڈین بولر گرنور برار کے جارحانہ رویے کو غیر پیشہ ورانہ قرار دیتے ہوئے اس پر کڑی تنقید کی۔

stories.title: Pakistan Aims for Global Investment and Value Addition in Mining Sector
stories.summary:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir announced on Friday that Pakistan is striving to become a competitive hub for long-term mineral investment. Speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad, CDF Munir assured international delegations and exhibitors that comprehensive security measures would cover the entire mining ecosystem, protecting infrastructure, projects, and personnel. He emphasized that the nation's objective extends beyond exporting raw materials to developing a full value chain encompassing refining and manufacturing.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, addressing the same two-day event, expressed optimism that Pakistan could achieve the status of the world's sixth-largest economy before 2050. He highlighted that the production of copper and gold at the Reko Diq project along the Tethyan belt is scheduled to begin in 2028 after a two-decade delay. The prime minister reiterated his commitment to halting raw mineral exports, urging investors to establish local refineries, smelters, and manufacturing facilities to create sustainable economic value and local jobs.

To facilitate international investors, the government is working to simplify administrative procedures, eliminate bureaucratic red tape, and ensure transparency through the digitisation of records and the National Minerals Data Centre. PM Sharif promised that federal and provincial administrations would coordinate closely to provide reliable infrastructure, power, and logistical support, while also emphasizing that safety and environmental protection remain paramount responsibilities.

Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik also addressed the forum, noting that Pakistan's mineral exploration efforts are increasingly focused on strategic resources for global markets. He stated that these initiatives are supported by modern geochemical and geophysical surveys, exploratory drilling, and upgraded geoscience advanced research laboratories designed to attract international partnerships.

stories.title: Karachi Faces Water Shortage Due to Maintenance Shutdown at Dhabeji Station
stories.summary:
Karachi is experiencing a daily water deficit of approximately 130 million gallons per day (MGD) following a 14-hour maintenance shutdown initiated by K-Electric at the Dhabeji Pumping Station on Friday. According to a spokesperson for the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC), the power supply suspension began at 10 am and is scheduled to last until midnight, affecting multiple pump houses across the facility.

The power outage rendered nine out of the 21 pumps at Dhabeji temporarily non-operational, while the remaining 12 pumps maintained partial operations. While Karachi typically receives a daily supply of around 650 MGD, the disruption caused overall supplies to drop to about 520 MGD. Meanwhile, water distribution from the Hub Pumping Station continued without interruption.

The temporary shortfall has impacted numerous areas across the city, including Landhi, Korangi, Malir, Shah Faisal, Gulshan, Clifton, Saddar, and Lyari. Towns such as Jinnah, Chanesar, Liaquatabad, and North Karachi are also affected, while Nazimabad and Gulberg are facing partial disruptions. Additionally, the Landhi and Sherpao hydrants remain closed throughout the duration of the maintenance work.

The KWSC spokesperson stated that water supply from the Dhabeji facility will be increased gradually once regular electricity is restored to the station.

stories.title: Mauricio Pochettino Set to Take Over as Manchester United Manager
stories.summary:
Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly finalizing a two-and-a-half-year contract to manage Manchester United through 2029, following the dismissal of Michael Carrick. The 54-year-old manager, currently serving as the head coach of the United States men's national team, is expected to complete his upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti before transitioning to Old Trafford.

US Soccer has reportedly agreed to release Pochettino, with the federation set to receive a total compensation package of $12 million for the departure of both the head coach and his coaching staff. Carrick's departure on Thursday followed a difficult start to the season that left the 20-time English champions in the Premier League relegation zone after securing only one victory in their opening 10 matches. Carrick becomes the seventh permanent manager dismissed by the club since the retirement of Alex Ferguson in 2013.

Pochettino brings extensive Premier League managerial experience from his previous stints at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, and Chelsea, alongside a tenure at Paris Saint-Germain. Earlier this year, he guided the United States to the last 16 of the World Cup and subsequently signed an extension through the 2030 tournament before accepting the position in Manchester.

Among the initial challenges awaiting Pochettino is resolving the future of club captain Bruno Fernandes, whose contract situation remains uncertain after he reportedly rejected a second extension offer. Manchester United's next fixture is a high-profile match against rival Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

stories.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole $400 Million via AI Deepfakes
stories.summary:
North Korean state-backed hackers have stolen more than $400 million over the past 18 months using a deceptive social engineering scheme known as "FaceStealer," according to the FBI. The law enforcement agency reported on Thursday that the hackers employ identity theft and AI-powered deepfake video calls to trick victims into trusting them. During these fabricated meetings, the attackers introduce a fake technical error that prompts targets to click on links or installation prompts, ultimately downloading malware. The scheme targets individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors and has ensnared even experienced technical users by exploiting trust in video conferencing platforms and personal relationships.

Brett Leatherman, the FBI's Cyber Branch Operations Director, noted that the North Korean regime relies on these large-scale cryptocurrency thefts to finance its unlawful weapons program. This announcement follows a recent FBI accusation that Pyongyang-affiliated hackers stole $6 billion from the cryptocurrency platform Binance, an allegation that North Korea denies. Patrick Grandy, assistant director at the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, emphasized the effectiveness of the FaceStealer campaign, which operates by leveraging contact lists, social media, and communication apps to impersonate victims and trap subsequent targets. As part of its investigation, the FBI has seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to victims of the FaceStealer operation.

stories.title: Deadly Militant Attacks Highlight Severe Vulnerability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police
stories.summary:
At least 12 policemen were martyred and more than a dozen others injured in a single day of relentless militant violence across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), underscoring the extreme risks faced by the provincial security force. Ten officers lost their lives during an ambush in Kohat as they returned from a joint clearance and anti-illegal gold mining operation with the civil administration in the Darbukach area. Security accounts indicate the police fought back against a large group of attackers, killing at least 18 of them. In a separate incident, two more officers were killed when a police patrol came under fire in Swabi, while an explosive-laden pickup truck targeted a police station gate in Dera Ismail Khan but was successfully repelled without causing police casualties.

Official data reveals that attacks on the KP police rose by 34 percent in the first half of the year, with fatalities and injuries doubling compared to the previous year. This growing lethality, combined with existing shortfalls in personnel, arms, and protective equipment, leaves the frontline force heavily exposed while combating insurgents who challenge state authority daily. Although October brought a temporary drop in attack numbers, Wednesday's violence demonstrates the fragility of those security gains. With the central government now overseeing the province, it bears the responsibility of ensuring the KP police receive requested funding, filled vacancies, armored vehicles, night-vision devices, better weapons, and necessary intelligence and military support during high-risk operations.

stories.title: Pakistan Draws First Test Against Sri Lanka After Saud Shakeel's 97 and Weather Interruption
stories.summary:
Pakistan secured a draw against Sri Lanka in the first Test on Friday in Rawalpindi, aided by a resilient 97-run knock from Saud Shakeel and multiple interruptions due to bad light. Sri Lanka had entered the fifth and final day in a strong position, reducing Pakistan to 151-5 at lunch with a lead of 139 after claiming four early wickets in the first session. However, Shakeel partnered with Ghazi Ghori for a crucial 92-run sixth-wicket stand following a brief 20-minute bad light delay before lunch. Shakeel, who also scored 93 in the first innings, fell just short of a century when he was bowled by Lahiru Kumara. Pakistan ultimately finished their second innings at 284-8, establishing a lead of 272 before both teams agreed to end the match.

The fixture was significantly affected by poor light conditions across the first four days, resulting in the loss of 117 overs out of the scheduled 360. Sri Lanka had squandered an opportunity on day four by losing their final six wickets to collapse from 404-6 to 446 all out in response to Pakistan’s declared total of 434-9, a collapse sparked by debutant pacer Saqib Khan's figures of 7-130. Earlier on the final morning, Babar Azam extended his century drought to 42 Test innings after scoring 34, falling to a leg-side catch off Milan Rathnayaka, who finished as Sri Lanka's top bowler with 3-47. Both squads will now contest the second and final Test at the same venue starting Tuesday, while Karachi separately faced a 130 MGD water shortfall due to annual maintenance at the Dhabeji Pumping Station by K-Electric.

stories.title: Transsion Holdings Plans to Expand Smartphone and Component Manufacturing Operations in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Chinese conglomerate Transsion Holdings is planning to broaden its manufacturing presence in Pakistan beyond simple smartphone assembly to encompass component production and deeper localization. During a meeting in Pakistan, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and Transsion Holdings Founder and Chairman George Zhu discussed the company’s ongoing operations, future investments, and strategies to strengthen the local industrial ecosystem. Transsion Holdings is the parent company of prominent smartphone brands such as Tecno and Infinix, operating locally through a China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) joint venture named Transsion Tecno Electronics.

During the discussions, the company presented an overview of its footprint in Pakistan across the smartphone, electric bike, and energy storage sectors. Both sides explored the potential for transitioning toward greater value addition and supporting local supply chains, which would create opportunities for domestic businesses and help position Pakistan as a regional manufacturing and export hub. Finance Minister Aurangzeb emphasized that macroeconomic stability provides a reliable foundation for long-term business planning, reiterating the government's commitment to structural reforms, export-oriented growth, and global supply chain integration. Zhu highlighted Pakistan as a strategic market owing to its large consumer base, geographical advantages, and favorable business environment, with both parties agreeing to maintain institutional engagement to advance these investment goals.

stories.title: International Energy Agency Reports Global Oil Market Returning to Surplus
stories.summary:
The International Energy Agency announced on Friday that the global oil market is shifting back to a surplus in the fourth quarter. This change is driven by Middle East exports recovering faster than global demand, despite ongoing shipping attacks. Previously, the Paris-based agency had forecast a supply deficit for the fourth quarter. Following the report, oil prices fell slightly, with Brent crude down 0.1% at $95.71 a barrel.

The agency reported that total oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, exceeding forecast demand by 1.7 million barrels per day. Gulf oil producers have increased exports since the war in Iran began in late February by utilizing workarounds like dark crossings through the Strait of Hormuz to avoid attacks. Additionally, OPEC+ pumped 41.23 million bpd in October, reaching 97% of its pre-war February volume.

To help ease market tightness, the IEA provided more details on its emergency reserve release, stating that 71 million barrels will be made available by the end of February, including 15 million barrels of diesel. The organization also suggested that members assess the need for additional diesel releases. High oil prices have further contributed to curbing demand this year, helping transition the market into a surplus.

Looking ahead, global oil demand is projected to drop by 2.7 million barrels per day in 2026 to 102.3 million bpd before increasing by 2 million bpd in 2027. Production is also expected to rise from nations outside OPEC+, including the United States, Canada, Brazil, Argentina, and Guyana, which will add 1.6 million bpd this year. By 2027, global supply is projected to reach 108.1 million bpd, resulting in a supply surplus of approximately 3.8 million bpd.

stories.title: Field Marshal Asim Munir Stresses Benefits for Local Communities at Forum
stories.summary:
Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir emphasized that mines and mineral development must provide tangible benefits to local communities during his address on Friday. Speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad, the Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces stated that Pakistan intends to become a competitive hub for long-term mineral investment and seeks to unlock the nation's mineral wealth as a collective national objective.

To safeguard the industry, the field marshal noted that security forces are implementing comprehensive measures to protect the entire mining ecosystem. This includes ensuring the safety of mines, miners, investments, industries, projects, and personnel associated with the sector. He stressed the importance of moving past raw exports toward value-added growth, noting that Pakistan aims to develop the entire value chain from refining to manufacturing alongside forming sustainable international partnerships.

Highlighting the human element, the field marshal praised Pakistanis as hardworking and courageous people who act as the primary source of strength for achieving national aspirations. He reiterated that developing the country's mineral resources requires sustained investment, long-term partnerships, and cooperative national efforts to turn potential into actual production.

Meanwhile, in Karachi, a water shortfall of approximately 130 million gallons per day occurred as K-Electric initiated annual maintenance work at the Dhabeji Pumping Station on Friday. The maintenance required a temporary suspension of power supply to multiple pump houses, according to a spokesperson for the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Suspends December Local Government Election Schedule
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court suspended the Election Commission of Pakistan's notification for local government elections in the federal capital. Justice Omer Majid Malik issued the stay order on Friday while hearing a petition filed by citizen Amjad Ali, halting the polls that had been scheduled for December 20.

During the hearing, Advocate Adil Aziz Qazi argued on behalf of the petitioner that the ECP had overlooked legal requirements while managing the electoral process, despite its legal obligation to ensure free, fair, and transparent elections. Accepting the request for suspension, the court issued notices to the ECP and other relevant respondents, directing them to submit detailed replies by November 26.

The court order effectively pauses the election schedule issued on October 21 until the respondents present their responses. This decision adds to a lengthy history of delays for Islamabad's local governance. The last local government elections in the federal capital took place in 2015, and the constitutional term of the elected body expired in February 2021.

Over the past five years, residents have remained without elected local representatives due to repeated legislative amendments, altered union council counts, and frequent schedule changes. The ECP had previously re-announced the December 20 polling date following the withdrawal of a February 15, 2026 schedule, which was postponed due to a Presidential Ordinance altering local government structures.

stories.title: Financial and Industrial Stocks Cause Sri Lankan Shares to Close Lower
stories.summary:
Sri Lankan shares closed lower on Friday, pushed down primarily by losses in financial and industrial stocks. The CSE All-Share index finished the session down 0.6% at 22,024.18 points. Among the biggest drags on the index were Hatton National Bank and Richard Pieris, which dropped 1.9% and 6.2%, respectively.

Despite the downward pressure on index values, market activity increased during the session. Trading volume rose to 100.7 million shares, up from 87.1 million shares in the previous trading session.

Market turnover also saw an increase, climbing to 3.23 billion Sri Lankan rupees, equivalent to approximately $9.71 million, compared to 2.98 billion rupees previously.

Exchange data revealed a split in investor participation during the session. Foreign investors acted as net buyers, acquiring stocks valued at 56.7 million rupees, whereas domestic investors operated as net sellers, offloading shares worth 3.21 billion rupees.

stories.title: Pakistan Short-Term Inflation Rises to 11.21 Percent Due to Perishable Food Costs
stories.summary:
Short-term inflation in Pakistan climbed to 11.21 per cent year-on-year for the week ending November 12, according to official figures released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics on Friday. The calculation is based on the Sensitive Price Index, which monitors 51 essential items across 50 markets in 17 cities. During the surveyed week, prices for 19 commodities increased, nine dropped, and 23 remained unchanged. The double-digit inflation rate was driven largely by increases in perishable food items and liquefied petroleum gas.

The index showed that items recording the highest week-on-week price hikes included tomatoes at 12.06 per cent, eggs at 5.98 per cent, potatoes at 2.42 per cent, garlic at 1.76 per cent, and chicken at 1.32 per cent. Conversely, notable price declines were observed for petrol down 7.42 per cent, diesel down 6.10 per cent, and onions down 1.70 per cent. On an annual basis, items like liquefied petroleum gas surged by 111.35 per cent, tomatoes by 78.94 per cent, and electricity for the first quarter by 52.38 per cent.

Energy costs continue to fuel inflationary pressures and indirectly boost sales tax collections through higher prices for everyday goods and services. This dynamic reflects cost-push inflation, placing mounting financial pressure on households. While petroleum and diesel prices have begun a slow decline over recent consecutive days, their impact will only appear in subsequent reviews. Previously, short-term inflation stood at 12.31 per cent year-on-year.

The tracking of these weekly metrics provides a detailed look at how price fluctuations in both food and non-food categories impact the cost of living. The continuous monitoring helps economists and policymakers understand consumer market pressures across the country. Official data collection remains vital for evaluating short-term economic shifts as households navigate fluctuating commodity values.

stories.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams, and Copilot Services
stories.summary:
Microsoft’s Outlook, Teams, and Copilot experienced a major global outage lasting over 12 hours due to server issues, disrupting communications for businesses and governments worldwide. The tech giant stated it was implementing fixes more broadly to achieve a persistent recovery and noted it was not aware of any malicious activity. The disruption affected government agencies in Australia, Japan, and the United States, alongside trading firms and airlines.

In Europe, stock exchange operator Euronext reported email communication hurdles, while British insurer Aviva activated backup plans for earnings calls. Danish shipping company Maersk warned customers of delayed updates, and US artificial intelligence firms OpenAI and Anthropic encountered problems with Microsoft connectors. Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air, and Air India also saw their email support services impacted by the technical failure.

The incident caused significant operational hurdles in Taiwan, where fund management at securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies was disrupted. One Taiwanese financial entity canceled a bond repurchase transaction, while another resorted to using a fax machine to confirm trades. In the United States, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its financial results, and Switzerland's Richemont briefly delayed its earnings announcement.

This event marks the second major disruption to hit Microsoft’s 365 services this year, following previous issues in January and October of last year. Analysts noted that while customers are unlikely to abandon the Microsoft ecosystem immediately, recurring reliability problems give IT departments reason to reconsider depending on a single provider. Government officials, including Australian Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke and Japanese Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki, confirmed that authorities and information system infrastructures were actively dealing with the email-related fallout.

stories.title: چینی محققین کا برقی کنگھی سے موروثی گنج پن کا علاج دریافت کرنے کا دعویٰ
stories.summary:
چین کے محققین نے موروثی گنج پن کے موثر علاج کے لیے ایک نئی ’برقی کنگھی‘ تیار کرنے کا دعویٰ کیا ہے، جس کی تحقیق سائنسی جریدے نیچر کمیونیکیشنز میں شائع ہوئی ہے۔ اس آلے کا نام ’ڈی ٹینگل‘ رکھا گیا ہے، جو کہ سنہ 2010 کی اینی میٹڈ فلم ’ٹینگلڈ‘ سے متاثر ہو کر رکھا گیا ہے۔

موروثی گنج پن، جسے سائنسی زبان میں اینڈروجینیٹک ایلوپیشیا کہا جاتا ہے، دنیا بھر میں ڈیڑھ سے دو ارب افراد کو متاثر کرتا ہے جس میں بالوں کی جڑیں کمزور ہو کر سکڑ جاتی ہیں۔ گنج پن کے علاج میں روایتی دواؤں اور سوئیوں کے استعمال کے مسائل کے پیش نظر محققین نے ایک ایسی کنگھی بنائی ہے جس کے دندانوں میں الیکٹروڈز نصب ہیں تاکہ دوائیں اور ضروری مادے براہ راست بالوں کی جڑوں تک پہنچائے جا سکیں۔

یہ کنگھی سر کی جلد پر ایک عارضی اور طاقتور برقی میدان پیدا کرتی ہے جو خلیات کی بیرونی تہہ کو متاثر کر کے علاجی اجزا کو تقریباً 660 مائیکرومیٹر گہرائی تک پہنچانے میں مدد دیتی ہے۔ اس برقی تحریک کا مقصد بالوں کی جڑوں تک خون کی فراہمی بڑھانا اور بال گرنے کے ذمہ دار حیاتیاتی عمل کو کم کرنا ہے۔

فی الحال یہ تجربات انسانوں کے بجائے گنج پن کے شکار چوہوں پر کیے گئے ہیں۔ نتائج کے مطابق برقی تحریک اور بالوں کی نشوونما کے اجزا کے مشترکہ استعمال سے چوہوں میں ایک ماہ کے اندر متاثرہ حصوں پر تقریباً مکمل بال دوبارہ اگ آئے، تاہم اس کے انسانوں کے لیے محفوظ اور مؤثر ہونے کا فیصلہ مزید طبی آزمائشوں کے بعد ہی کیا جائے گا۔

stories.title: Tata Motors Reports Quarterly Loss Driven by Jaguar Land Rover Restructuring Costs
stories.summary:
India-based Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles announced a consolidated net loss for the July-September quarter on Friday, weighed down by exceptional restructuring charges at its luxury British unit, Jaguar Land Rover. The company reported a second-quarter consolidated loss of 55.31 billion rupees, or approximately $587.48 million, contrasting sharply with a profit of 761.7 billion rupees during the same period in the previous year. Exceptional charges for the quarter totaled 67.38 billion rupees.

The Jaguar Land Rover unit has been navigating recovery following a cyberattack that previously disrupted production and sales. Additionally, the automaker is undertaking an extensive restructuring program encompassing asset impairments and employee separation costs. Despite these bottom-line losses and pressures on margins and cash generation, Tata Motors posted a consolidated revenue rise to 969.20 billion rupees, up from 723.49 billion rupees in the corresponding period last year.

The automaker's financial results contrast with domestic peers Maruti Suzuki and Hyundai Motor India, which reported declines in quarterly profits, while Mahindra and Mahindra recorded an increase. JLR's overall performance remains a critical element for Tata Motors' financial health and overall profitability. Meanwhile, the parent company, Tata Sons, faces an internal governance dispute regarding the reappointment of chairman N. Chandrasekaran, as majority shareholder Tata Trusts opposes the board's decision.

stories.title: Paytm Secures Preliminary Central Bank Approval for Wallet Licence
stories.summary:
India's digital financial services provider Paytm has obtained preliminary approval from the central bank for its payments services unit to issue prepaid payment products, including digital wallets. Announced on Friday, this in-principle clearance permits Paytm Payments Services to operate its wallet business independently from Paytm Payments Bank, which previously housed the service for years. After receiving final authorization from the Reserve Bank of India, the company will be allowed to offer prepaid payment instruments to its customers.

Market analysts view the development as an indication of easing regulatory friction that brings positive market sentiment. Anand Dama, executive director and head of banking and financial services research at Nuvama Institutional Equities, noted that the licence will create new revenue avenues, such as a prepaid card business. However, because this is only an initial approval, the final licence will take time, meaning any potential revenue impact will likely not materialize until the financial year 2028. Following the announcement, Paytm shares climbed up to 1.8 percent to 1,960 rupees before closing 0.8 percent higher on Friday, pushing the stock up nearly 50 percent for the year due to robust business growth.

Paytm originally launched its digital wallet business in 2014, growing it into the largest digital wallet provider nationwide before transferring operations to Paytm Payments Bank in 2017 to comply with regulatory requirements. The business faced severe setbacks in 2022 when the Reserve Bank of India prohibited the bank from onboarding new customers. Regulatory scrutiny intensified in 2024 as the central bank restricted the bank from accepting fresh deposits, credits, and top-ups for existing accounts and wallets because of persistent non-compliance and supervisory issues, effectively halting regular wallet loading. These accumulated restrictions ultimately led to the cancellation of the bank's licence earlier this year and its subsequent winding up.

stories.title: Copper Hits Four-Month Low Amid Fifth Consecutive Weekly Drop
stories.summary:
Copper prices declined to their lowest level in nearly four months on Friday, marking the metal's fifth consecutive weekly drop amid growing anxieties surrounding artificial intelligence investments. Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange dipped 0.5 percent to $13,519 per metric ton after touching $13,456 earlier in the session, its weakest price point since July 17. The industrial metal faced a 1.8 percent loss for the week, extending a downward trajectory that began in mid-October.

According to Goldman Sachs analysts, London Metal Exchange copper prices have dropped about 7 percent over the past month to $13,588 per ton, largely driven by volatility in artificial intelligence-related equities following a Democratic sweep in the United States midterm elections. Investor caution deepened further after the unexpected resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday. Goldman Sachs attributed the recent price correction primarily to positioning rather than deteriorating fundamentals, noting that positioning could remain subdued if equity markets begin pricing in an earlier deceleration in artificial intelligence capital spending while data center construction proceeds.

Despite the global sell-off, physical supply remains constrained in top consuming nation China, where local inventories are low and import premiums are high. Copper stockpiles within Shanghai Futures Exchange warehouses contracted by an additional 18.3 percent this week to reach 27,642 tons, representing the lowest volume since December 23. Furthermore, the Yangshan copper premium, which serves as a gauge for Chinese import appetite, reached a record $285 per ton on Friday. Other base metals also trended downward alongside a strong United States dollar, with aluminium, zinc, lead, and nickel all seeing losses, while tin emerged as the sole gainer by rising 0.9 percent to $47,080 per ton.

stories.title: Gold Prices in Pakistan Decrease Following International Market Losses
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan experienced a downward correction on Friday, following a similar downward trend observed in the international market. Rates shared by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association indicate that the local market price of gold dropped by Rs4,900 per tola during the day, bringing the new price to Rs411,636 per tola. In addition, the price for 10 grams of gold fell by Rs4,201, resulting in a selling price of Rs352,911.

This drop follows even sharper declines recorded on the previous day. On Thursday, the price of gold per tola fell significantly by Rs10,900, reaching Rs416,536. The domestic reductions mirror movements on the global stage, where the international rate of gold decreased by $49, settling at $3,891 per ounce.

Alongside the yellow metal, the local silver market also saw a downward adjustment on Friday. The price of silver dropped by Rs111, reaching a total of Rs5,467 per tola according to the data provided by the association.

stories.title: Islamabad Constable Arrested for Accepting Bribe to Free Beggar
stories.summary:
Islamabad Capital Territory Police arrested Constable Afzal Ahmed for allegedly taking a bribe to let a female beggar escape from custody. The arrest highlights the department's firm stance against internal corruption.

Authorities registered a case against the officer at the Ramna Police Station following the incident. He will now go through formal legal proceedings.

Senior Superintendent of Police Operations Qazi Ali Raza stated that corrupt personnel will receive no leniency and face both departmental and legal consequences. He emphasized that nobody stands above the law in the department.

The SSP stressed that exploiting the police uniform for personal gain remains completely unacceptable. Officials whose actions harm the force's reputation have no place in the organization.

Internal accountability will persist across the agency to maintain discipline and transparency. Any employee caught abusing their authority will face punishment regardless of their rank.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Up Slightly Against US Dollar
stories.summary:
The Pakistani rupee posted a marginal increase against the US dollar within the inter-bank market. The local currency finished the session at 276.60, rising by Re0.01 compared to the previous day's close of 276.61.

Globally, the US dollar remained near a 19-month peak following strong weekly gains. Speculation grew regarding a potential larger interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve, while Treasury yields climbed after remarks from US President Donald Trump regarding Iran.

The euro hovered near its lowest valuation against the dollar since April 2025, while the Japanese yen stayed close to the key 160 threshold. Japanese officials indicated readiness to address excessive currency volatility if necessary.

Meanwhile, international oil prices declined slightly and headed toward a second weekly loss. Brent futures dropped to $95.54 a barrel, and US West Texas Intermediate futures fell to $88.18 a barrel amid developments involving the US blockade of Iran.

The dollar index stood at 103.17, maintaining levels not seen since April 2025. Investors also monitored ongoing developments in global equity markets, particularly surrounding technology sector pressures.

stories.title: جادو ٹونے سے حکومتیں نہیں ملتیں، عظمیٰ بخاری کا سخت ردعمل
stories.summary:
پنجاب کی وزیر اطلاعات عظمیٰ بخاری کا کہنا ہے کہ نہ تو جادو ٹونے سے حکومتیں چلتی ہیں اور نہ ہی جھوٹ اور پروپیگنڈے سے حکومتیں گرتی ہیں۔ اپنے ایک بیان میں انہوں نے کہا کہ کچھ بے روزگار اور سیاسی یتیم نئے ٹھکانے تلاش کرنے کی خاطر ہاتھ پاؤں مار رہے ہیں لیکن پنجاب میں ترقی کا سفر تیزی سے جاری ہے۔

عظمیٰ بخاری کا مزید کہنا تھا کہ وزیراعلیٰ پنجاب مریم نواز نے گڈ گورننس، شفافیت اور میرٹ کو پنجاب کا ماڈل بنا دیا ہے جو اب دوسرے صوبوں کے لیے ایک مثال بن چکا ہے۔ انہوں نے دعویٰ کیا کہ پچھلے دو سالوں میں جو کام مریم نواز نے کر دکھائے ہیں وہ ملکی تاریخ میں پہلے کبھی نہیں ہوئے اور جعلی بیانیے بنانے والے اب قصہ پارینہ بن چکے ہیں۔

صوبائی وزیر نے کہا کہ مریم نواز کو ٹارگٹ کرنے والے غیر اہم لوگ خود کو اہم بنانے کی کوشش کر رہے ہیں مگر ان کی کوئی دال نہیں گلنے والی کیونکہ عوام انہیں کھلے دل سے تسلیم کر چکے ہیں۔ انہوں نے اس بات پر بھی زور دیا کہ مردہ گھوڑے میں ہوا بھرنے کی اب کوئی بھی کوشش کامیاب نہیں ہو سکتی۔

stories.title: کراچی: چینی انجینئرز پر حملہ کرنے والے مجرم کو 48 سال قید
stories.summary:
کراچی کی انسداد دہشتگردی عدالت نے گل بائی کے قریب چینی انجینئرز کی گاڑی پر فائرنگ کے مقدمے کا فیصلہ سناتے ہوئے مرکزی ملزم داد بخش کو مجموعی طور پر 48 برس قید کی سزا سنا دی ہے۔ ڈپٹی پراسیکیوٹر جنرل کے مطابق ملزم نے اپنے ساتھیوں کے ہمراہ جولائی 2021 میں اس حملے کو انجام دیا تھا جس کے نتیجے میں ایک چینی انجینئر زخمی ہوا تھا۔

عدالت نے ملزم کو 7 لاکھ روپے جرمانہ ادا کرنے کا حکم دینے کے علاوہ ساڑے آٹھ لاکھ روپے زخمی غیر ملکی شہری کو معاوضے کے طور پر دینے کا بھی حکم جاری کیا۔ فیصلے میں کہا گیا کہ استغاثہ نے شواہد کی بنیاد پر یہ ثابت کیا کہ ملزم نے دانستہ طور پر چینی انجینئرز کی گاڑی کو نشانہ بنایا تھا۔
